title: Wire AppRootIPad detail column for threads, podcasts, sources, search
description: Update AppRootIPad.swift detail column to observe navigationModel.selectedThread, selectedEpisode, selectedSource, and selectedArticle and render the appropriate detail view (ThreadDetailView, PodcastPlayerView, ArticleListView/ArticleDetailView) in landscape. Refactor TodayIPadView to project brief detail into the NavigationSplitView detail column instead of its internal HStack split.
acceptance_criteria: Tapping a thread in ThreadsIPadView shows ThreadDetailView in detail column
Tapping an episode in PodcastsIPadView shows PodcastPlayerView in detail column
TodayIPadView no longer uses internal HStack split in landscape
Portrait behaviour unchanged for all views

handoff_summary.completed: Added `selectedBrief: Brief?` to `iPadNavigationModel`. Replaced the `Text("Select an item")` placeholder in `AppRootIPad.swift` detail column with a section-aware `detailContent` `@ViewBuilder` that renders `ThreadDetailView`, `BriefDetailView`, `PodcastPlayerView`, `ArticleListView`, or `ArticleDetailView` based on `navigationModel.selectedSection` and whichever selection is non-nil, falling back to a `ContentUnavailableView` prompt. Removed `TodayIPadView`'s internal `landscapeLayout` HStack (which had its own detail pane); in landscape the view now renders only the brief list, setting `navigationModel.selectedBrief` on tap; the `AppRootIPad` detail column renders `BriefDetailView` from that value. Portrait remains a `NavigationStack` with `NavigationLink` rows, unchanged. Build: **BUILD SUCCEEDED**.
handoff_summary.remaining: None for this bead. Downstream: SearchIPadView already sets `navigationModel.selectedArticle` — article detail in search is wired by this bead's `detailContent`. SettingsIPadView is a future bead. Deep-link routing to `iPadNavigationModel` (spec Task 9) and QA pass (Task 10) are separate beads.
handoff_summary.risks: Portrait `NavigationStack` in `TodayIPadView` and the `NavigationStack` wrappers in `detailContent` must not conflict with `NavigationSplitView`'s implicit stacks. In practice SwiftUI's split view detail column hosts its own implicit stack, and wrapping with an explicit `NavigationStack` is the standard pattern for resetting navigation when the selection changes — this matches the pattern used in `ThreadsIPadView` portrait mode. Monitor for unexpected double-stack navigation bars during QA.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester should verify: (1) tapping a thread in landscape shows ThreadDetailView in the right column; (2) tapping an episode in landscape shows PodcastPlayerView; (3) tapping a brief in landscape shows BriefDetailView without the old HStack layout; (4) portrait pushes navigation within each section's own NavigationStack unchanged; (5) no double navigation bars appear in the detail column.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None expected. All changes are additive to AppRootIPad and a pure refactor of TodayIPadView. No sibling beads touch these files. NavigationModel.swift gains one field which is backward-compatible.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Detail column uses explicit `NavigationStack` wrappers around each detail view (e.g. `NavigationStack { ThreadDetailView(...) }`). This resets navigation state when the user picks a new item, prevents stale back-stacks from bleeding across selections, and is consistent with how Apple's NavigationSplitView + detail column pattern works when the detail content changes identity. An alternative (no NavigationStack wrapper) would leave NavigationSplitView to provide the implicit stack, but then `navigationTitle` modifiers on detail views would not render correctly. For `TodayIPadView`, `selectedBrief` was moved from local `@State` to `iPadNavigationModel.selectedBrief` so the AppRootIPad detail column can observe it without prop-drilling — consistent with how threads, episodes, and feed selections are already managed.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: Tester should verify: landscape thread tap → ThreadDetailView appears in detail column (not a new full-screen push); landscape episode tap → PodcastPlayerView appears; landscape brief tap → BriefDetailView appears (old HStack is gone); sources feed/source selection → ArticleListView appears; search article selection → ArticleDetailView appears; switching sections clears the detail column (shows ContentUnavailableView); portrait NavigationStack push still works for all sections; iPhone layout is pixel-identical (AppRoot.swift horizontalSizeClass branch guards all of this).
handoff_summary.known_limitations: Settings section has no supplementary content list (the `sectionContent` switch still shows a `ContentUnavailableView` for settings) — this is intentional per spec; a full SettingsIPadView is deferred. `UIScreen.main` deprecation warnings in SourcesIPadView and PodcastsIPadView are pre-existing and not introduced by this bead.

conflict_risks: None expected. All changes are additive to AppRootIPad and a pure refactor of TodayIPadView. No sibling beads touch these files. NavigationModel.swift gains one field which is backward-compatible.

execution_history.summary: Wired the AppRootIPad detail column to render section-appropriate detail views based on iPadNavigationModel state, and refactored TodayIPadView to eliminate its internal HStack landscape split.

guardrails.template_text:
# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
